title: hybrid-deferred-insert-ring-allocator-with-hopscotch-pinning-and-opportunistic-compaction
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce fragmentation and eviction thrash in the paged KV block manager under mixed workloads (short prefix storms + long-running streams). The existing freelist + softpin heuristics still show tail latency spikes when hot prefixes rotate rapidly. This PR introduces a hybrid 'deferred-insert ring allocator' combined with a lightweight hopscotch-style pinning layer and opportunistic in-band compaction windows coordinated with the continuous-batching scheduler.

What it does (high level): 1) Deferred-insert ring allocator: new ring-backed allocation path for transient hot allocations. Newly freed blocks are appended to a per-core ring; the allocator defers re-inserting these blocks into the global freelist for a short epoch, favoring reuse for recently-seen hot prefixes and reducing global freelist churn. 2) Hopscotch pinning: lightweight near-neighbor pin metadata is attached to blocks that belong to the same prefix hotset; eviction tries short-distance swaps before evicting a pinned block to reduce thrash. 3) Opportunistic compaction windows: the scheduler exposes low-utilization windows (derived from continuous-batching idle intervals) where background compaction can run without impacting critical request latencies. Compaction only touches candidate spans identified by a new 'frag-score' heuristic. 4) Scheduler integration: the allocator exposes a tiny admission signal so the batching scheduler can postpone large compaction or reclaim batches when tail latency constraints are tight.

Implementation notes: - New files: kv/allocator/ring_allocator.{cc,h}, kv/allocator/hopscotch_pin.{cc,h}, kv/allocator/compact_worker.{cc,h}. Integration glue added to kv/cache_manager.cc to wire epochs and metrics. - Hopscotch metadata is 2 bytes per block (packed): a hint pointer and an age tag. The hopscotch swap path is bounded (max 4 hops) to keep eviction cost stable. - Deferred insert ring is per-CPU with power-of-two sizing and lock-free push/pop. Rings are drained periodically into the global freelist during compaction windows or when ring fullness exceeds threshold. - New config knobs: allocator.defer_epoch_ms (default 20ms), allocator.ring_size (per-core default 4096), allocator.hop_slots (default 4), allocator.compact_batch_tokens (default 32k).

Benchmarks (internal perf lab): workload=chat-mix-16k (50% short prefix, 30% long streams, 20% embeddings). Compared to main @ 2024-11-01: - P50 latency: -3% (minor) - P95 latency: -18% - P99 latency: -32% - Throughput (tokens/sec at same 99% SLO headroom): +12% - Global freelist contention metric (contention_cycles): -67% - Average fragment score per node: -45% These gains are most pronounced when prefix churn is high. Small regression windows observed at extreme steady-state long-stream-only workloads (+1-2% CPU) due to hopscotch bookkeeping.

Testing and safety: - Unit tests for ring allocator (push/pop races, wraparound) and hopscotch swap correctness. - Stress tests in perf-canary with mixed load for 72 hours. - Added a runtime feature flag (allocator.ring_enabled) defaulting to true in canaries; rollout plan includes staged enablement and immediate rollback signal if latency regressions >5% on P99.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-4129) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Benchmarks attached - [x] Runtime knob + metrics - [x] Rollout plan

Why different from previous allocators: this approach biases reuse towards recent frees (good for hot-rotating prefixes) without permanently bypassing the global allocator; hopscotch pinning reduces eviction-of-hot-object cases without large metadata overhead. Opportunistic compaction keeps steady-state fragmentation low without adding periodic high-latency GC pauses.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Nice approach — can you explain why 20ms was chosen for defer_epoch_ms? We saw earlier that 50ms worked better for large batch workloads.

Avery Chen (author): Chose 20ms after perf sweep; it's a tradeoff point where ring reuse captures short prefix rotations without causing long-term starvation. Added a config knob and documentation note so SREs can tune to 50ms in heavy batch-only clusters.
Priya Nair: Please add a metric for ring-utilization and an alertable signal. Also we need a safety timeout to force-drain rings during low-memory OOM pressure.
Avery Chen (author): Added allocator.ring_utilization and allocator.ring_force_drain_on_oom config; updated integration tests to exercise force-drain path.
Liam O'Connor: The hopscotch swap path looks potentially cache-unfriendly on NUMA nodes — have you validated cross-node costs?
Avery Chen (author): We bound swaps to 4 hops and keep metadata compact; added a NUMA-aware test and a note in ops/allocator.md recommending ring_size reduction for cross-NUMA deployments.
Priya Nair: CI flake on macOS build; looks unrelated but please investigate.
Avery Chen (author): Fixed a portability constexpr issue and re-ran CI.
merge_info: merged by squash-merge on 2024-11-21 by Priya Nair (merge commit: squash). Release note entry added.
release_notes: Introduce a hybrid deferred-insert ring allocator + hopscotch pinning to reduce KV cache fragmentation and eviction thrash. Improves P99 latency in high prefix-churn workloads; tunable knobs added for operators.
